passages.provision_quote: In an action against a defendant who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence that is alleged to have caused a harm to the plaintiff, it shall not be a defense, and the defendant may not assert, that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.
passages.note: Single-subject chaptered bill she authored; its whole operative section is AI liability for harm.

rows.reasoning: Krell authored AB 316 (2025-2026), a single-subject act adding Civil Code 1714.46, whose operative section bars a defendant who "developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence" from asserting "that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff." That operative content is the rung "Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm": it keeps liability on the developer instead of the system. It imposes no pre-deployment testing in high-stakes areas and no government approval before deployment, so the rungs above it are excluded, and as binding law it excludes the voluntary-guidelines and no-interference rungs.
